30.s_dismas: Suppoſe, thou diddeſt deſire to goe to thy freinds, and hadeſt a longing to thy fathers houſe: why dideſt thou ſteale my goddes?
30.odr_com: Suppose, thou diddest desire to goe to thy freinds, and hadest a longing to thy fathers house: why didest thou steale my godds?
30.sabates_a: Suppose thou didst desire to go to thy friends, and hadst a longing to thy father's house, why didst thou steal my gods?
30.madueke_b: Suppose thou didst desire to go to thy friends, and hadst a longing to thy father's house, why didst thou steal my gods?

31.s_dismas: Iacob anſwered: In that I departed vnwitting to thee, I feared leſt thou wouldeſt take away thy daughters by force.
31.odr_com: Iacob answered: In that I departed vnwitting to thee, I feared lest thou wouldest take away thy daughters by force.
31.sabates_a: Jacob answered: In that I departed unwitting to thee, I feared lest thou wouldst take away thy daughters by force.
31.madueke_b: Jacob answered: In that I departed unwitting to thee, I feared lest thou wouldst take away thy daughters by force.

32.s_dismas: But wheras thou chargeſt me with theft: with whom ſoeuer thou ſhalt find thy goddes, let him be ſlaine before our brethren. Search, what ſoeuer of thy things thou ſhalt finde with me, and take away. Saying this, he knew not that Rachel had ſtollen the idols.
32.odr_com: But wheras thou chargest me with theft: with whom soeuer thou shalt find thy goddes, let him be slaine before our brethen. search, what soeuer of thy things thou shalt finde with me, and take away. Saying this, he knew not that Rachel had stollen the idols.
32.sabates_a: But whereas thou chargest me with theft; with whom soever thou shalt find thy gods, let him be slain before our brethren: search whatsoever of thy things thou shalt find with me, and take away. Saying this, he knew not that Rachel had stolen the idols.
32.madueke_b: But whereas thou chargest me with theft; with whom soever thou shalt find thy gods, let him be slain before our brethren: search whatsoever of thy things thou shalt find with me, and take away. Saying this, he knew not that Rachel had stolen the idols.

33.s_dismas: Laban therfore hauing gone into the tent of Iacob, and of Lia, and of both the hand-maides, found them not. And when he was entred into Rachels tent,

33.madueke_b: Laban therefore having gone into the tent of Jacob, and of Lia, and of both the handmaids, found them not. And when he was entered into Rachel's tent,

34.s_dismas: ſhe in haſt hid the idols vnder the camels litter, and ſatte therupon: and when he had ſought al the tent, and found nothing,
34.odr_com: she in hast hid the idols vnder the camels litter, and satte therupon: and when he had sought al the tent, and found nothing,
34.sabates_a: she in haste hid the idols under the camel's litter, and sat thereupon: and when he had sought all the tent, and found nothing,
34.madueke_b: she in haste hid the idols under the camel's litter, and sat thereupon: and when he had sought all the tent, and found nothing,

35.s_dismas: she ſaid: Let not my lord be angrie that I can not riſe vp before thee, becauſe according to the cuſtome of wemen it is now chanced to me. So his carefulnes in ſeeking was deluded.
35.odr_com: she said: Let not my lord be angrie that I can not rise vp before thee, because according to the custome of wemen it is now chanced to me. so his carefulnes in seeking was deluded.
35.sabates_a: she said: Let not my lord be angry that I cannot rise up before thee, because according to the custom of women it is now chanced to me. So his carefulness in seeking was deluded.
35.madueke_b: she said: Let not my lord be angry that I cannot rise up before thee, because according to the custom of women it is now chanced to me. So his carefulness in seeking was deluded.

36.s_dismas: And Iacob being angrie ſaid in chiding maner: For what fault of myne, and for what offence of my part haſt thou ſo chaſſed after me,
36.odr_com: And Iacob being angrie said in chiding maner: For what fault of myne, and for what offence of my part hast thou so chaffed after me,
36.sabates_a: And Jacob being angry said in chiding manner: For what fault of mine, and for what offence of my part hast thou so chased after me,
36.madueke_b: And Jacob being angry said in chiding manner: For what fault of mine, and for what offence of my part hast thou so chased after me,

37.s_dismas: and ſearched al my houshould ſtuffe? What haſt thou found of al the ſubſtance of thy houſe? lay it here before my brethren, and thy brethren, and let them iudge betwen me & thee.
37.odr_com: and searched al my houshould stuffe? What hast thou found of al the sabstance of thy house? lay it here before my brethren, and thy brethren, and let them iudge betwen me & thee.
37.sabates_a: and searched all my household-stuff? What hast thou found of all the substance of thy house? Lay it here before my brethren, and thy brethren, and let them judge between me and thee.
37.madueke_b: and searched all my household-stuff? What hast thou found of all the substance of thy house? Lay it here before my brethren, and thy brethren, and let them judge between me and thee.

38.s_dismas: Haue I therfore bene with thee twentie yeares? thy ewes and goates were not barren, the wethers of thy flocke I did not eate:
38.odr_com: Haue I therfore bene with thee twentie yeares? thy ewes and goates were not barren, the wethers of thy flocke I did not eate:
38.sabates_a: Have I therefore been with thee twenty years? Thy ewes and goats were not barren, the wethers of thy flock I did not eat:
38.madueke_b: Have I therefore been with thee twenty years? Thy ewes and goats were not barren, the wethers of thy flock I did not eat:

39.s_dismas: neyther that which the beaſt had caught did I shew to thee, I made good al the damage: whatſoeuer periſhed by theft, thou dideſt exact it of me:
39.odr_com: neyther that which the beast had caught did I shew to thee, I made good al the damage: whatsoeuer perished by theft, thou didest exact it of me:
39.sabates_a: neither that which the beast had caught did I shew to thee, I made good all the damage: whatsoever perished by theft thou didst exact it of me:
39.madueke_b: neither that which the beast had caught did I shew to thee, I made good all the damage: whatsoever perished by theft thou didst exact it of me:

40.s_dismas: day and night was I parched with heate, and with froſt, and ſleepe did flye from myne eyes.
40.odr_com: day and night was I parched with heate, and with frost, and sleepe did flye from myne eyes.
40.sabates_a: day and night was I parched with heat, and with frost, & sleep did fly from mine eyes.
40.madueke_b: day and night was I parched with heat, and with frost, & sleep did fly from mine eyes.

41.s_dismas: And in this ſorte haue I ſerued thee in thy houſe twentie yeares, fourtene for thy daughters, and ſix for thy flockes: thou haſt changed alſo my wages tenne times.
41.odr_com: And in this sorte haue I serued thee in thy house twentie yeares, fourtene for thy daughters, and six for thy flockes: thou hast changed also my wages tenne times.
41.sabates_a: And in this sort have I served thee in thy house twenty years, fourteen for thy daughters, and six for thy flocks: thou hast changed also my wages ten times.
41.madueke_b: And in this sort have I served thee in thy house twenty years, fourteen for thy daughters, and six for thy flocks: thou hast changed also my wages ten times.

42.s_dismas: Vnles the God of my father Abraham, and the feare of Iſaac had holpe me, peraduenture now thou haddeſt ſent me away naked: God beheld my affliction and the laboure of my hands, and rebuked thee yeſterday.
42.odr_com: Vnles the God of my father Abraham, and the feare of Isaac had holpe me, peraduenture now thou haddest sent me away naked: God beheld my affliction and the laboure of my hands, and rebuked thee yesterday.
42.sabates_a: Unless the God of my father Abraham, and the fear of Isaac had holpen me, peradventure now thou hadst sent me away naked: God beheld my affliction and the labour of my hands, and rebuked thee yesterday.
42.madueke_b: Unless the God of my father Abraham, and the fear of Isaac had holpen me, peradventure now thou hadst sent me away naked: God beheld my affliction and the labour of my hands, and rebuked thee yesterday.

43.s_dismas: Laban anſwered him: The daughters are mine and the children, and thy flockes, and al things that thou ſeeſt are mine: what can I do to my daughters, and nephews?
43.odr_com: Laban answered him: The daughters are mine and the children, and thy flockes, and al things that thou seest are mine: what can I do to my daughters, and nephews?
43.sabates_a: Laban answered him: The daughters are mine and the children, and thy flocks, and all things that thou seest are mine: what can I do to my daughters, and nephews?
43.madueke_b: Laban answered him: The daughters are mine and the children, and thy flocks, and all things that thou seest are mine: what can I do to my daughters, and nephews?

44.s_dismas: Come therfore, let vs enter in league: that it may be for a teſtimonie betwen me and thee.
44.odr_com: Come therfore, let vs enter in league: that it may be for a testimonie betwen me and thee.
44.sabates_a: Come therefore, let us enter in league: that it may be for a testimony between me and thee.
44.madueke_b: Come therefore, let us enter in league: that it may be for a testimony between me and thee.

45.s_dismas: Iacob therfore tooke a ſtone, and erected it for a title:
45.odr_com: Iacob therfore tooke a stone, and erected it for a title:
45.sabates_a: Jacob therefore took a stone, and erected it for a title:
45.madueke_b: Jacob therefore took a stone, and erected it for a title:

46.s_dismas: and he ſaid to his brethren: Bring hither ſtones. Who gethering them together made a heape, and they did eate vpon it:
46.odr_com: and he said to his brethren: Bring hither stones. Who gethering them together made a heape, and they did eate vpon it:
46.sabates_a: and he said to his brethren: Bring hither stones. Who gathering them together made a heap, and they did eat upon it:
46.madueke_b: and he said to his brethren: Bring hither stones. Who gathering them together made a heap, and they did eat upon it:

47.s_dismas: which Laban called The witneſſe heape: and Iacob called The hillock of teſtimonie, either of them according to the proprietie of his language.
47.odr_com: Which Laban called The witnesse heape: and Iacob called The hillock of testimonie, either of them according to the proprietie of his language.
47.sabates_a: Which Laban called the witness-heap: and Jacob called the hillock of testimony, either of men according to the property of his language.
47.madueke_b: Which Laban called the witness-heap: and Jacob called the hillock of testimony, either of men according to the property of his language.

48.s_dismas: And Laban ſaid: This heape ſhal be a witnes betwen me and thee this day, and therfore the name therof was called Galaad, that is, The witnes heape.
48.odr_com: And Laban said: This heape shal be a witnes betwen me and thee this day, and therfore the name therof was called Galaad, that is, The witnes heape.
48.sabates_a: And Laban said: This heap shall be a witness between me and thee this day, and therefore the name thereof was called Galaad, that is, The witness-heap.
48.madueke_b: And Laban said: This heap shall be a witness between me and thee this day, and therefore the name thereof was called Galaad, that is, The witness-heap.

49.s_dismas: Our Lord behold and iudge betwen vs when we ſhal be departed one from the other,
49.odr_com: Our Lord behold and iudge betwen vs when we shal be departed one from the other,
49.sabates_a: Our Lord behold and judge us when we shall be departed one from the other,
49.madueke_b: Our Lord behold and judge us when we shall be departed one from the other,

50.s_dismas: if thou ſhalt afflict my daughters, and if thou bring in other wiues ouer them: none is witnes of our talke but God, who is preſent and beholdeth.
50.odr_com: if thou shalt afflict my daughters, and if thou bring in other wiues ouer them: none is witnes of our talke but God, who is present and beholdeth.
50.sabates_a: if thou shalt afflict my daughters, and if thou bring in other wives over them; none is witness of our talk but God, who is present and beholdeth.
50.madueke_b: if thou shalt afflict my daughters, and if thou bring in other wives over them; none is witness of our talk but God, who is present and beholdeth.

51.s_dismas: And he ſaid againe to Iacob: Behold this heape, and the ſtone which I haue erected betwen me and thee,
51.odr_com: And he said againe to Iacob: Behold this heape, and the stone which I haue erected betwen me and thee,
51.sabates_a: And he said again to Jacob: Behold this heap, and the stone which I have erected between me and thee,
51.madueke_b: And he said again to Jacob: Behold this heap, and the stone which I have erected between me and thee,

52.s_dismas: ſhal be a witnes: this heape, I ſay, and the ſtone be they for a teſtimonie, if either I ſhal paſſe beyond it, going towards thee, or thou ſhalt paſſe beyond it, thinking harme to me.
52.odr_com: shal be a witnes: this heape, I say, and the stone be they for a testimonie, if either I shal passe beyond it going towards thee, or thou shalt passe beyond it, thinking harme to me.
52.sabates_a: shall be a witness: this heap, I say, and the stone, be they for a testimony, if either I shall pass beyond it going towards thee, or thou shalt pass beyond it, thinking harm to me.
52.madueke_b: shall be a witness: this heap, I say, and the stone, be they for a testimony, if either I shall pass beyond it going towards thee, or thou shalt pass beyond it, thinking harm to me.

53.s_dismas: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nachor iudge betwen vs, the God of their father. Iacob therfore ſware by the feare of his father Iſaac:
53.odr_com: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nachor iudge betwen vs, the God of their father. Iacob therfore sware by the feare of his father Isaac:
53.sabates_a: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nachor judge between us, the God of their father, Jacob therefore sware by the fear of his father Isaac:
53.madueke_b: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nachor judge between us, the God of their father, Jacob therefore sware by the fear of his father Isaac:

54.s_dismas: and after he had offred victimes in the mountaine, he called his brethren to eate bread. Who when they had eaten, lodged there:
54.odr_com: and after he had offred victimes in the mountaine, he called his brethren to eate bread. Who when they had eaten, lodged there:
54.sabates_a: and after he had offered victims in the mountain, he called his brethren to eat bread. Who when they had eaten, lodged there.
54.madueke_b: and after he had offered victims in the mountain, he called his brethren to eat bread. Who when they had eaten, lodged there.

55.s_dismas: but Laban ariſing in the night, kiſſed his ſonnes, and daughters, and bleſſed them: and returned vnto his place.
55.odr_com: but Laban arising in the night, kissed his sonnes, and daughters, and blessed them: and returned vnto his place.
55.sabates_a: but Laban arising in the night, kissed his sons, and daughters, and blessed them: and returned unto his place.
55.madueke_b: but Laban arising in the night, kissed his sons, and daughters, and blessed them: and returned unto his place.

janvier_by_verse.1: After he heard the words of Laban's sons saying: Jacob hath taken all that was our father's, and being enriched of his substance, is become great:
janvier_by_verse.2: and perceiving also Laban's countenance, that it was not towards him as yesterday and the other day,
janvier_by_verse.3: especially our Lord saying to him: Return into the land of thy fathers, and to thy kindred, and I will be with thee;
janvier_by_verse.4: he sent, and called Rachel and Lia into the field where he fed the flocks,
janvier_by_verse.5: and said to them: I see your father's countenance that it is not towards me as yesterday and the other day: and the God of my father hath been with me.
janvier_by_verse.6: And yourselves know that I have served your father to the uttermost of my power.
janvier_by_verse.7: Yea your father also hath circumvented me, and hath changed my wages ten times: and yet God hath not suffered him to hurt me.
janvier_by_verse.8: If at any time he said: They of diverse colours shall be thy wages; all the sheep brought forth young of diverse colours. But when he said contrary: Thou shalt take all the white ones for thy wages; all the flocks brought forth white ones.
janvier_by_verse.9: And God hath taken your father's substance, and given it to me.
janvier_by_verse.10: For after the time came of the ewes conceiving, I lifted up mine eyes, and saw in my sleep the males ascending upon the females of diverse colours, and the spotted, and the speckled.
janvier_by_verse.11: And the Angel of God said to me in sleep: Jacob? And I answered: Here I am.
janvier_by_verse.12: Who said: Lift up thine eyes, and see all the males ascending upon the females, them of diverse colours, the spotted and the speckled. For I have seen all things that Laban hath done to thee.
janvier_by_verse.13: I am the God of Bethel, where thou didst anoint the stone, and didst vow the vow unto me. Now therefore arise, and go out of this land, returning into the land of thy nativity.
janvier_by_verse.14: And Rachel and Lia answered: Have we any thing left in the goods and heritage of our father's house?
janvier_by_verse.15: Hath he not reputed us as strangers, and sold us, and eaten up the price of us?
janvier_by_verse.16: But God hath taken our father's riches, and delivered them to us, and to our children: wherefore do all things that God hath commanded thee.
janvier_by_verse.17: Jacob therefore rose up, and setting his children and wives upon camels, went his way.
janvier_by_verse.18: And he took all his substance, and flocks, and whatsoever he had gotten in Mesopotamia, and went forward to Isaac his father into the land of Chanaan.
janvier_by_verse.19: At that time Laban was gone to shear his sheep, and Rachel stole the idols of her father.
janvier_by_verse.20: And Jacob would not confess to his father in law that he fled.
janvier_by_verse.21: And when he was gone as well himself as all things that were his right, & having passed the river was marching on to the Mount Galaad,
janvier_by_verse.22: it was told Laban the third day that Jacob fled.
janvier_by_verse.23: Who, taking his brethren unto him, pursued him seven days: and he overtook him in the Mount Galaad.
janvier_by_verse.24: And he saw in his sleep God saying unto him: Take heed thou speak not roughly any thing against Jacob.
janvier_by_verse.25: And Jacob had now pitched his tent in the mountain: and when he with his brethren had overtaken him, he pitched his tent in the same Mount Galaad.
janvier_by_verse.26: And he said to Jacob: Why didst thou so, that unwitting to me thou wouldst carry away my daughters as captives with the sword?
janvier_by_verse.27: Why wouldst thou fly without my knowledge, and not tell me, that I might have brought thee on the way with joy, and songs, and timbrels, and citterns?
janvier_by_verse.28: Thou hast not suffered me to kiss my sons and daughters: thou hast done foolishly: now also indeed,
janvier_by_verse.29: my hand is able to requite thee evil: but the God of your father said unto me yesterday: Take heed thou speak not any thing against Jacob roughly.
janvier_by_verse.30: Suppose thou didst desire to go to thy friends, and hadst a longing to thy father's house, why didst thou steal my gods?
janvier_by_verse.31: Jacob answered: In that I departed unwitting to thee, I feared lest thou wouldst take away thy daughters by force.
janvier_by_verse.32: But whereas thou chargest me with theft; with whom soever thou shalt find thy gods, let him be slain before our brethren: search whatsoever of thy things thou shalt find with me, and take away. Saying this, he knew not that Rachel had stolen the idols.
janvier_by_verse.33: Laban therefore having gone into the tent of Jacob, and of Lia, and of both the handmaids, found them not. And when he was entered into Rachel's tent,
janvier_by_verse.34: she in haste hid the idols under the camel's litter, and sat thereupon: and when he had sought all the tent, and found nothing,
janvier_by_verse.35: she said: Let not my lord be angry that I cannot rise up before thee, because according to the custom of women it is now chanced to me. So his carefulness in seeking was deluded.
janvier_by_verse.36: And Jacob being angry said in chiding manner: For what fault of mine, and for what offence of my part hast thou so chased after me,
janvier_by_verse.37: and searched all my household-stuff? What hast thou found of all the substance of thy house? Lay it here before my brethren, and thy brethren, and let them judge between me and thee.
janvier_by_verse.38: Have I therefore been with thee twenty years? Thy ewes and goats were not barren, the wethers of thy flock I did not eat:
janvier_by_verse.39: neither that which the beast had caught did I shew to thee, I made good all the damage: whatsoever perished by theft thou didst exact it of me:
janvier_by_verse.40: day and night was I parched with heat, and with frost, & sleep did fly from mine eyes.
janvier_by_verse.41: And in this sort have I served thee in thy house twenty years, fourteen for thy daughters, and six for thy flocks: thou hast changed also my wages ten times.
janvier_by_verse.42: Unless the God of my father Abraham, and the fear of Isaac had holpen me, peradventure now thou hadst sent me away naked: God beheld my affliction and the labour of my hands, and rebuked thee yesterday.
janvier_by_verse.43: Laban answered him: The daughters are mine and the children, and thy flocks, and all things that thou seest are mine: what can I do to my daughters, and nephews?
janvier_by_verse.44: Come therefore, let us enter in league: that it may be for a testimony between me and thee.
janvier_by_verse.45: Jacob therefore took a stone, and erected it for a title:
janvier_by_verse.46: and he said to his brethren: Bring hither stones. Who gathering them together made a heap, and they did eat upon it:
janvier_by_verse.47: Which Laban called the witness-heap: and Jacob called the hillock of testimony, either of men according to the property of his language.
janvier_by_verse.48: And Laban said: This heap shall be a witness between me and thee this day, and therefore the name thereof was called Galaad, that is, The witness-heap.
janvier_by_verse.49: Our Lord behold and judge us when we shall be departed one from the other,
janvier_by_verse.50: if thou shalt afflict my daughters, and if thou bring in other wives over them; none is witness of our talk but God, who is present and beholdeth.
janvier_by_verse.51: And he said again to Jacob: Behold this heap, and the stone which I have erected between me and thee,
janvier_by_verse.52: shall be a witness: this heap, I say, and the stone, be they for a testimony, if either I shall pass beyond it going towards thee, or thou shalt pass beyond it, thinking harm to me.
janvier_by_verse.53: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nachor judge between us, the God of their father, Jacob therefore sware by the fear of his father Isaac:
janvier_by_verse.54: and after he had offered victims in the mountain, he called his brethren to eat bread. Who when they had eaten, lodged there.
janvier_by_verse.55: but Laban arising in the night, kissed his sons, and daughters, and blessed them: and returned unto his place.
